story: You rented the flat from Tan Ah Kow and paid him a $2,600 deposit on 3 August 2025, with the agreement stating he must refund it within 14 days after you move out, minus any damage. You moved out on 31 July 2026, left the keys in the mailbox as he told you to, and cleaned the flat, and he replied "Received" and said "ok, all good. will transfer deposit after i check." The 14 days was up on 14 August 2026, but on 15 August 2026 he said the sofa had a scratch and refused to return the deposit, and even after you asked him on 20 August 2026 to send a photo of the scratch and to return the $2,600 if there was no damage, he still has not paid you back.
summary:
On 3 Aug 2025, I signed a tenancy agreement with my landlord, Mr Tan Ah Kow, for an HDB flat. I paid him a security deposit of $2,600 by bank transfer. The agreement says he must refund the deposit within 14 days after I move out, minus any damage cost.

On 31 Jul 2026, I moved out. I cleaned the flat and left the keys in the mailbox as he told me to. He replied "ok, all good" and said he would transfer the deposit after checking the flat.

checks.text: Your claim fits a CJTS category: lease not exceeding 2 years (residential premises), refund of rental deposit.
You are claiming $2,600. The limit is $20,000, or $30,000 if both sides agree.
Date of cause of action: 15 Aug 2026, when the landlord refused. You have 2 years, so until 15 Aug 2028.
The landlord is in Singapore, so the claim can be served.

scta_schedule.title: Small Claims Tribunals Act 1984, s 5(1) and the Schedule (specified claims)

scta_s2.title: Small Claims Tribunals Act 1984, s 2(1) (prescribed limit) and s 5(3)-(4)

scta_s5_time.title: Small Claims Tribunals Act 1984, s 5(3)(b) (2-year limit)
scta_s5_time.quote:
5.—(3) Except where this Act expressly provides otherwise, the jurisdiction of a tribunal does not extend to a claim —
(a) the value of which exceeds the prescribed limit; or
(b) after the expiry of 2 years after the date on which the cause of action accrued.
scta_s5_time.guide: State Courts, A Guide to Small Claims, p.4: "All claims must be filed within two years after the date the cause of action accrued. A cause of action is the fact or facts which entitles you, in law, to start a court action against the Respondent. You may file a claim in the civil courts, e.g. at the Magistrates' Courts if the cause of action accrued more than 2 years ago."

scta_s5_service.title: Small Claims Tribunals Act 1984, s 5(1)(b) (served in Singapore)
scta_s5_service.quote:
5.—(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, a tribunal has the jurisdiction to hear and determine any claim which —
(a) is a specified claim; and
(b) is served in Singapore on the respondent under section 19(1).
scta_s5_service.guide: Judiciary, Cases eligible for a small claim: the tribunals cannot hear a claim where the respondent is outside Singapore, because the claim cannot be served on anyone outside Singapore.

blindspots.intro: Things that could exist and are not in your files yet: what the landlord may hold, and what you may have missed. Listed so you are not surprised at the Consultation. We do not argue his case.
blindspots.note: He can file a counterclaim for damage on CJTS up to 3 days before the Consultation. Your evidence sheet is your answer to it.

questions.q: Could he have his own photos of the sofa, taken after you left?
questions.hint: Your move-out video (E5) shows the sofa at 1:12. Keep it.

questions.q: Has he sent, or could he get, a repair or cleaning invoice?
questions.hint: Ask for it in your written request. On CJTS a Defects Schedule form lists each defect and its cost.

questions.q: Did you sign an inventory or handover form?
questions.hint: Your agreement, cl. 6, says there is one. Get your copy. If it notes the sofa, it matters either way.

questions.q: Were there any other agreed conditions, spoken or in messages on any channel? Cleaning, repainting, bills, keys.
questions.hint: Check SMS, email and other apps you used with him. Anything agreed can change what he can hold back.

questions.q: Did anyone else see the handover? A friend, mover or agent.
questions.hint: Witnesses go on the Submission for Hearing form on CJTS.

questions.q: Did you accept any deduction, even in passing?
questions.hint: If yes, say how much and when. It changes the amount you claim.

next_steps.title: Send a written request for the deposit
next_steps.note: Your biggest gap. Give him 7 days to reply. The draft uses only your facts and your agreement.

next_steps.title: Gather what is missing
next_steps.note: Stamp duty certificate, signed inventory list, final bill, dated move-in photos.

next_steps.title: Pre-filing assessment on CJTS
next_steps.note: Pick the category, enter the refusal date and the amount, answer the questions. The ID it gives you lasts 7 days.

next_steps.title: Fill the claim form and pay
next_steps.note: Six parts: you, him, the claim, a summary of at most 500 characters, documents (PDF only, 5MB each, with page numbers), money order. Singpass login. Then pick a Consultation date.

next_steps.title: Serve him within 7 working days
next_steps.note: Save the Respondent Copy from CJTS, hand it to him or send by registered post, then file the Declaration of Service.

next_steps.title: Before the Consultation
next_steps.note: He may open e-Negotiation (5 rounds). Fill the Submission for Hearing form: events in date order, witnesses. Bring E1 to E6 in evidence sheet order.
